methodological_conclusions: An ordinary pulled-back scalar Hessian contains both Jacobian-Hessian-Jacobian and Euler-gradient times second-field-map terms.
The second-map-gradient term can be linear in the retained field-redefinition coefficient, and vanishes at stationarity or for affine maps.
Transform background/external source couplings consistently; away-from-minimum propagation requires tadpole contributions.
Classical pulled-back functionals and ordinary quantum Legendre effective actions require different transformation statements.
Retain interaction sources in the full action and track induced EFT orders; published basis inventories do not supply the current coefficients.
limitations: Only named body sections were checked; no complete paper or supplement was exhaustively reviewed.
Most returned papers received abstract-level screening only.
No nonlocal field-map formalism, all-order tadpole resummation, Vilkovisky-DeWitt action or quantum mean-field transformation was implemented.
No published loop coefficient, beta matrix, finite matching result or older phenomenological bound was imported.
Scalar formulas do not replace ordered Grassmann derivatives or the packet-specific convention conversion.
